task: A new manager asks you what stonewalling is and how to take a time-out instead. Explain both to them in two sentences.
model: Stonewalling means going quiet or pulling away without saying why, so the other person feels ignored. To take a time-out, you tell them you need one, agree on when you'll come back, and then come back.

ideas.heading: Stonewalling
ideas.body: Stonewalling is going silent, withdrawing or changing the subject without saying why. The other person feels ignored or rejected.
ideas.label: Stonewalling is withdrawing without saying why.
ideas.met: You explained that stonewalling means going silent or withdrawing.
ideas.unsure: It's unclear whether you explained stonewalling. Describe what the person does.

ideas.heading: Taking a time-out
ideas.body: Tell the other person you need a time-out, instead of going silent. For example, "I need ten minutes to think about this."
ideas.label: You tell the other person you need a time-out.
ideas.met: You said to tell the other person you need a time-out.
ideas.unsure: It's unclear whether you said to announce the time-out. Say that you tell the other person you need one.

ideas.heading: Coming back
ideas.body: A time-out ends when you come back. Agree on when you'll return to the conversation, then do it.
ideas.label: You agree on when to come back, and then come back.
ideas.met: You said to agree on when to come back, and then come back.
ideas.unsure: It's unclear whether you said when to come back. Say that you agree on a time, so the other person isn't left waiting.
